) engine=InnoDB;

  INDEX(name),

) engine=InnoDB;

  password VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL ,

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"

        postcode:
          title: Postcode

            four digits and, when the owner's city maps to a known region
            (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), must fall within that
            region's inclusive range (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099).

            returned when supplied.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'

      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:

        - type: object
          properties:

              readOnly: true

              title: Initials
              description: >-

              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>', where REGION
                is the region code derived from the postcode and HASH8 is the first 8
                upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over (normalizedTelephone +
                lastName).
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                A single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits of the
                customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>',
                where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by all owners that belong to the same
                household (i.e. that have the same last name and address). Owners who
                knowingly share a household - created with 'sharesHousehold' true -
                are assigned the same value.
              type: string
              example: 'a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The owner's derived identity key, formatted
                '<normalizedTelephone>|<email-or-empty>|<householdId>'. Duplicate
                detection is expressed solely through this key: a create is
                rejected with 409 Conflict only when the whole key exactly matches
                an existing owner's. The household segment is the shared household
                id when the owner belongs to a shared household, otherwise empty.
              type: string
              example: '+61400000001|george.franklin@example.com|a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of owners that already existed, at the time this owner
                was created, sharing the same first and last name
                (case-insensitively). Zero when the name was unique on create.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level, assigned on creation. Starts
                at 1, gains 1 when an email address is present, gains a further 1
                when the name was unique on create (namesakeCount is 0), and is
                capped at 3. Level 4 is reserved for tenure.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's locality (region), taken from the REGION segment of the
                customerCode (the region derived from the postcode when the owner was
                created). 'UNKNOWN' when no region could be derived.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:

              items:

              readOnly: true
          required:

## Summary

I implemented soft-match ("possible duplicate") detection for owner creation. When a new owner is not a hard duplicate but shares an existing owner's `lastName` and `postcode` with a *different* telephone, it's still created and flagged.

Changes:

1. **`Owner.java`** — added two persisted fields, `possibleDuplicate` (Boolean) and `possibleDuplicateOf` (Integer), with columns `possible_duplicate` / `possible_duplicate_of` and their getters/setters.

2. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — in `addOwner`, after the existing hard-duplicate rejection, I compute the soft match and set both fields on the owner before it's saved. New helper `findPossibleDuplicate(owner)` matches an existing owner by case-insensitive `lastName` + equal `postcode` + different normalized `telephone` (only when a postcode was supplied), returning the earliest (lowest-id) match or `null`. `possibleDuplicate` is set to `true`/`false` accordingly, so the "otherwise false" case is explicit.

3. **`openapi.yml`** — added read-only `possibleDuplicate` (boolean) and `possibleDuplicateOf` (int32) to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries them and MapStruct auto-maps them by name.

4. **Schema SQL** (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `postgres`, `mysql`) — added the two new columns to the `owners` table.

5. **`hsqldb/data.sql`** — the seed rows use column-less `INSERT INTO owners VALUES (...)`, so I added the two matching `NULL` values to each of the 10 rows to keep the column count aligned (this was the cause of the initial "row column count mismatch" failure). The h2/postgres seeds use explicit column lists and needed no change.

The `coreFlagsPossibleDuplicate` acceptance test passes, and the full suite (`BUILD SUCCESS`) is green.
